headline: Wednesday's the window; the break's slid south to Rosa Flats
body:
A small-craft advisory covers the channel from 3 PM through this evening, and the outer waters past Santa Rosa stay under advisory through Wednesday morning. Tuesday starts workable inside the triangle — light NW at dawn, seas near 3 ft — but W wind fills to 12 kn by midafternoon and the ride home stiffens. Wednesday is the cleaner day: channel winds go light and seas run 2–4 ft close in.

On temperature, the break isn't in the triangle. All three corners read warm — west 71.2, east 71.1 — with only the south point, in Santa Cruz Basin, cooling to 69. That's the corner to start, though it's still a shade warm of the 64–68 band. The true break has slid off toward Santa Rosa Flats, sitting right on the 68 line (68.9 today, 68.7 tomorrow). But Rosa is blown out today and carries 6 ft of leftover swell tomorrow — a hard run for marginal seas, not clean water. Fish the south point Wednesday and watch that basin edge for a cooler push.
